title: Project Tesseract
description: A top-down monster-collecting RPG where you capture Hakkos with Tesseracts and challenge Arena bosses.
prompt:
You are an expert game developer specializing in browser-based games.
Your task is to create a complete, playable monster-collecting RPG from this single specification.
The game’s public working title is Project Tesseract.
The creatures in this world are called Hakkos.
The game should feel inspired by classic top-down Game Boy Advance and Nintendo DS-era monster-collecting RPGs, particularly in its sense of exploration, turn-based battles, towns, routes, visible wild creatures, dialogue, progression, and nostalgic pixel-art presentation.
However, the game must be an original work with its own terminology, creatures, locations, lore, visual identity, mechanics, and code.
Do not copy copyrighted characters, creature designs, maps, dialogue, music, names, logos, or assets from Pokémon or any other existing franchise.
The result should be a functional and enjoyable single-player browser game that demonstrates the full gameplay loop.

1. PRIMARY OBJECTIVE
Create a playable game that allows the player to:
1.	Start a new game.
2.	Choose or enter a save name.
3.	Control a character named Coal.
4.	Wake up in a starter village.
5.	Speak to Coal’s mother.
6.	Visit a local Hakko researcher.
7.	Choose one of three original starter Hakkos.
8.	Build an active deck of up to five Hakkos.
9.	Explore a top-down pixel-art world.
10.	Encounter visible wild Hakkos away from the main paths.
11.	Battle wild Hakkos and trainers.
12.	Capture wild Hakkos using consumable Tesseracts.
13.	View the current capture probability before throwing a Tesseract.
14.	Level Hakkos through experience.
15.	Unlock new moves and abilities as Hakkos level.
16.	Evolve eligible Hakkos, with the player choosing whether evolution occurs.
17.	Visit towns, shops, Hakko Vets, storage areas, and Arenas.
18.	Defeat smaller trainers leading towards Arena bosses.
19.	Defeat five major Arena bosses.
20.	Earn one Arena Trophy from each boss.
21.	Unlock new towns and regions after each Arena victory.
22.	Complete Hakko Codex entries.
23.	Increase Scholar Rank through discovery and collection.
24.	Use Hakko abilities to access blocked and hidden areas.
25.	Defeat the final twin champions.
26.	Unlock a post-game quest involving a hidden Legendary Hakko.
27.	Save and reload progress.
The game may simplify scale where necessary, but every major system listed above should exist in functional form.

2. CORE DESIGN PHILOSOPHY
The central design rule is:
Every mechanic must encourage exploration, discovery, collection, growth, or attachment to the player’s Hakkos.
The four primary design pillars are:
Explore
The player should regularly leave the main path to find useful or interesting rewards.
Optional areas should contain things such as:
•	Rare Hakkos
•	Hidden items
•	Lore
•	Shortcuts
•	Tesseracts
•	Healing supplies
•	Legendary clues
•	Fishing spots
•	Mining locations
•	Secret paths
Discover
The world should reward curiosity.
Players should discover:
•	New Hakkos
•	New habitats
•	New towns
•	Optional routes
•	Hidden caves
•	Secret beaches
•	Ancient ruins
•	Rare encounters
•	Lore fragments
•	New traversal abilities
Collect
The player collects:
•	Hakkos
•	Arena Trophies
•	Codex entries
•	Scholar Rank progress
•	Tesseracts
•	Food
•	Healing items
•	Rare items
•	Legendary clues
Grow
Growth should occur through:
•	Hakko levels
•	New moves
•	Evolution
•	Better team composition
•	Stronger Tesseracts
•	Scholar Rank
•	World access
•	Arena progression
•	Codex completion

5. PLAYER CHARACTER
The player character is named Coal.
Coal is sixteen years old.
Sixteen is the legal age in this world to become a licensed Hakko Handler.
Coal is not a silent protagonist.
Coal may respond through simple dialogue choices such as:
•	Yes
•	No
•	Accept
•	Decline
•	Ask for more information
•	Leave
Coal begins the game in their bedroom in the starter village.
Coal’s visual design should be original, readable in pixel art, and suitable for a young adventurer.
Coal does not have combat statistics.
Coal’s progression comes from:
•	Their active Hakko deck
•	Their Hakko collection
•	Their Tesseract access
•	Their Arena Trophies
•	Their Scholar Rank
•	Their world traversal abilities

6. GAME STRUCTURE
The game should contain:
•	One starter village
•	Five additional major towns
•	Five Arenas
•	A final champion confrontation involving twins
•	Routes between towns
•	Optional side areas
•	Forests
•	Caves
•	Mountains
•	Beaches
•	Rivers
•	Swamps
•	Desert
•	Snow region
•	Volcano region
•	Ancient ruins
•	Abandoned laboratory or research site
•	Hidden Legendary locations
Progression should feel nostalgic and route-based.
The preferred progression flow is:
Town
↓
Route
↓
Secondary route or dungeon
↓
Arena access area
↓
Arena boss
↓
New route
↓
Next town
Each new sector should be blocked until the previous Arena boss is defeated.
Arena victories grant trophies and unlock access to the next sector.
Optional and hidden areas should branch away from the main route.
Some optional areas should initially be inaccessible and require a Hakko world ability such as:
•	Swim
•	Fly
•	Break rocks
•	Cut vines
•	Light dark caves
•	Clear fog
•	Push boulders
•	Dig
•	Climb cliffs
•	Melt ice
•	Burn dense vegetation
•	Repair bridges
•	Reveal hidden paths
•	Power ancient machines
•	Move heavy objects
•	Cross gaps
•	Detect spirits
•	Detect crystal passages
The player should be encouraged to return to earlier areas after gaining new abilities.

7. WORLD SCALE
The world should feel roughly comparable in scale to a compact GBA-era monster-collecting RPG.
For the tech demo, the world may use compact maps, but it must still create the impression of a connected region.
Use multiple maps rather than one enormous map.
Each town and route should have:
•	A unique visual theme
•	Distinct music or ambience
•	Relevant wild Hakkos
•	Trainers
•	NPC dialogue
•	Items
•	Clear exits
•	At least one optional discovery where practical
The game must not use global level scaling.
Early routes remain low level.
Late areas remain dangerous.
Returning to an early area with a high-level team should make the player feel powerful.

8. TOWN THEMES
Create six settlements total.
Use these themes as a foundation:
Starter Village
A peaceful rural village surrounded by grassland and light woodland.
Contains:
•	Coal’s home
•	Coal’s bedroom
•	Coal’s mother
•	Local Hakko researcher
•	Starter selection
•	Basic shop
•	Hakko Vet
•	Home storage
•	Trophy display area in Coal’s bedroom
•	Fast travel point after activation
Town One
Agricultural or forest-based town.
Arena specialises in a suitable natural element.
Town Two
Mining and mountain town.
Include caves and mining encounters.
Town Three
Desert or canyon settlement.
Include ruins, heat-based creatures, and open terrain.
Town Four
Swamp, river, coastal, or wetland settlement.
Include fishing and water traversal.
Town Five
Snow, volcanic, ancient, or high-technology settlement.
This should feel like the final major region before the champion confrontation.
You may choose the exact sequence, but the geography and difficulty curve must make sense.
Each town should contain at least a simplified version of:
•	Hakko Vet
•	Shop
•	Storage access
•	Fast travel point
•	Arena where applicable
•	Several NPCs
•	One or more hints about the next Arena’s element specialisation
•	Optional dialogue
•	A small number of side quests
The full design target is at least twenty NPCs per town, but for the playable tech demo you may use a smaller representative population while keeping the data system capable of supporting the full amount.

9. MAIN STORY
The main story is straightforward and should not rely on a central villain.
Coal wakes up on the day they become eligible to begin collecting Hakkos.
Coal’s mother encourages them to visit the local Hakko researcher.
The researcher gives Coal:
•	A Hakko Codex
•	A starting set of basic Tesseracts
•	A choice of one of three starter Hakkos
•	Basic guidance about Hakkos and Arenas
Coal’s goal is to become champion by defeating five Arena bosses.
Each Arena boss has a distinct personality and combat style.
Each Arena boss primarily specialises in one element.
The routes leading to each Arena contain smaller trainers who help teach the player about that region’s mechanics and elemental matchups.
There is no traditional evil organisation.
Conflict comes from:
•	Challenging trainers
•	Difficult environments
•	Strong wild Hakkos
•	Arena progression
•	Exploration hazards
•	Ancient mysteries
•	The final champions
After the fifth Arena Trophy is earned, Coal gains access to the final championship confrontation.
The final champions are twins.
The twins should each have:
•	A distinct personality
•	A different team identity
•	One Legendary Hakko in their standard line-up
•	A strong mixed team rather than a single-element team
The final encounter may be presented as sequential battles rather than simultaneous combat, because the core battle format is 1v1.
After Coal defeats both twins, Coal becomes champion.
The twins then reveal information about an old journal or ancient clue connected to a final hidden Legendary Hakko.
This opens the post-game Legendary quest.
NPCs across the world may gain new dialogue after the twins are defeated.
The final Legendary should not simply be handed to the player.
The player should follow clues across several towns and optional locations to discover where it sleeps.
Avoid complex timed puzzles.
Use exploration, dialogue clues, traversal abilities, and environmental discovery instead.

10. HAKKO CREATURE SYSTEM
Create at least fifty unique Hakkos.
All Hakkos must be original.
Each Hakko should have:
•	Unique name
•	Numeric Codex ID
•	Short visual description
•	Distinct silhouette
•	One or two elements
•	Base stats
•	Gender availability or gender ratio
•	Rarity
•	Habitat
•	Temperament
•	Evolution chain
•	Level-up move list
•	Up to six equipped moves
•	One or more world or passive abilities where appropriate
•	Favourite food
•	Spawn behaviour
•	Catch difficulty
•	Codex description
•	Normal colour design
•	Shiny colour design
•	Optional sound or cry description
A Hakko may have:
•	No evolution
•	One evolution
•	Two evolutions
Three total stages is the maximum.
Not every Hakko should evolve.
Some Hakkos should have only two stages.
Some should remain single-stage creatures and compensate through rarity, stats, abilities, or unique roles.
The player chooses whether to evolve an eligible Hakko.
Evolution should not be forced immediately.

11. HAKKO ECOSYSTEMS
Split Hakkos across ecosystems.
A reasonable target distribution is:
•	Forest
•	Grassland
•	Farm
•	River
•	Lake
•	Ocean
•	Beach
•	Cave
•	Mine
•	Mountain
•	Snow
•	Volcano
•	Desert
•	Swamp
•	Ruins
•	Abandoned laboratory
•	Night-only areas
•	Fishing encounters
•	Mining encounters
•	Tree encounters
•	Hidden or Legendary locations
Some Hakkos may appear in multiple related habitats.
Each habitat should have a balanced mix of:
•	Common Hakkos
•	Uncommon Hakkos
•	Rare Hakkos
•	Very rare Hakkos
•	Optional special encounters
Avoid overcrowding the first route with too many species.
Introduce new Hakkos steadily throughout progression.

12. HAKKO RARITY
Use a clear rarity system.
Recommended categories:
•	Common
•	Uncommon
•	Rare
•	Exceptional
•	Legendary
Legendary Hakkos should be extremely limited and story-relevant.
Shiny Hakkos are separate from rarity.
Any normal non-Legendary Hakko may potentially appear as a shiny variant.
Use a low but achievable shiny encounter chance.
For a tech demo, a rate between approximately 1 in 300 and 1 in 1000 is acceptable.
Choose a value that allows testing while still feeling special.
The shiny variant should:
•	Use one alternate colour design
•	Remain shiny through all evolutions
•	Have a visible shiny indicator
•	Have slightly improved potential or stats
•	Not be so much stronger that normal Hakkos become worthless
Each Hakko has only:
•	One normal colour design
•	One shiny colour design

13. HAKKO TEMPERAMENTS
Temperaments affect wild overworld behaviour, not combat stats.
Possible temperaments include:
•	Timid
•	Aggressive
•	Curious
•	Lazy
•	Playful
•	Protective
•	Territorial
•	Social
•	Pack-oriented
•	Solitary
•	Watchful
•	Mischievous
Examples:
•	Timid Hakkos move away from Coal.
•	Aggressive Hakkos may approach or chase Coal.
•	Curious Hakkos watch Coal and move closer slowly.
•	Lazy Hakkos may sleep.
•	Playful Hakkos may run in circles or move unpredictably.
•	Protective Hakkos remain near smaller Hakkos.
•	Territorial Hakkos stay within a defined area.
•	Pack Hakkos appear in groups.
Use simple state-driven movement rather than advanced simulation.
The goal is to make the world feel alive.

14. MASCOT HAKKO
Create one highly recognisable mascot Hakko.
The mascot should:
•	Be cute
•	Have a strong silhouette
•	Be visually simple enough for icons and menus
•	Be found early in the game
•	Not be one of the three starters
•	Be useful but not overpowered
•	Have expressive idle behaviour
•	Be suitable for the title screen, loading screens, Codex graphics, and promotional material
The mascot’s name and design must be original.

15. STARTER HAKKOS
Create three original starter Hakkos.
Do not simply use the standard Fire, Water, and Grass trio.
Use an original but understandable triangular relationship.
Possible examples include:
•	Ember / Tide / Bloom
•	Electric / Earth / Air
•	Metal / Crystal / Sound
•	Fire / Ice / Nature
•	Light / Shadow / Spirit
Choose a trio that produces a balanced strength-and-weakness cycle.
Each starter should:
•	Have three evolution stages
•	Have a strong personality
•	Be visually distinct
•	Be viable through the full game
•	Have at least one world ability
•	Gain several moves through levelling
•	Support different play styles
•	Have normal and shiny colour designs
The starter selection scene should show:
•	Name
•	Sprite or placeholder art
•	Elements
•	Short description
•	General battle style
•	Confirmation dialogue

16. ELEMENT SYSTEM
Use the following element pool:
•	Fire
•	Water
•	Earth
•	Nature
•	Electric
•	Ice
•	Air
•	Poison
•	Metal
•	Crystal
•	Light
•	Shadow
•	Psychic
•	Sound
•	Bug
•	Spirit
•	Void
Each Hakko may have up to two base elements.
Dual-element Hakkos should be less common than single-element Hakkos, but not extremely rare.
Create a coherent element chart containing:
•	Strengths
•	Weaknesses
•	Resistances
•	Immunities where appropriate
Avoid giving a Hakko two elements that directly undermine the creature’s intended identity.
Do not combine two elements on one Hakko when those elements are designed as direct opposites and the combination would create confusing or self-cancelling matchups.
Examples of combinations to avoid unless strongly justified:
•	Fire and Water
•	Light and Shadow
•	Nature and Poison, if Nature is defined as directly opposed to Poison
•	Ice and Fire
•	Spirit and Void, if they are defined as direct opposites
The exact chart should be balanced and easy to understand.
Use simple damage multipliers such as:
•	2.0x for strong
•	0.5x for resisted
•	0x for immune
•	1.0x for neutral
For dual-element defenders, combine multipliers sensibly.
Cap extreme multipliers if necessary to maintain balance.

17. HAKKO STATS
Use a simple stat system.
Recommended stats:
•	HP
•	Physical Attack
•	Physical Defence
•	Special Attack
•	Special Defence
•	Speed
Avoid:
•	IVs
•	EVs
•	Natures that modify stats
•	Breeding stats
•	Hidden gene systems beyond shiny inheritance through evolution
The goal is strategic clarity rather than competitive optimisation.
Each Hakko species should have a clear role, such as:
•	Fast physical attacker
•	Slow tank
•	Special attacker
•	Status specialist
•	Balanced fighter
•	Defensive support
•	High-risk attacker
•	Cooldown-focused controller

18. LEVELS AND EXPERIENCE
Maximum level is 100.
The entire active deck receives experience after a battle.
Experience distribution should work as follows:
•	Every conscious Hakko in the active deck receives a base share.
•	Hakkos that actively participated receive an additional bonus.
•	The Hakko that lands the final blow receives a second bonus.
A suggested distribution is:
•	Team base share: 50% of standard awarded experience
•	Participation bonus: additional 30%
•	Final-blow bonus: additional 20%
You may adjust the exact percentages for balance.
Do not award experience to fainted Hakkos unless you deliberately allow a reduced amount.
Levelling may grant:
•	Stat increases
•	New moves
•	Improved abilities
•	Evolution eligibility
•	Stronger passive effects
Show level-up feedback clearly.

19. MOVES AND ABILITIES
Each Hakko may equip up to six battle moves.
Moves are divided into:
•	Physical
•	Special
•	Status
•	Utility
Moves may have:
•	Power
•	Accuracy
•	Element
•	Cooldown
•	Priority
•	Status chance
•	Target restrictions
•	Special conditions
Do not use mana.
Basic moves may have no cooldown or a very short cooldown.
Stronger or more disruptive moves should use cooldowns.
Cooldowns should count down each turn.
A Hakko should not be able to repeatedly spam its strongest move.
Hakkos unlock additional moves through levelling.
The move-selection interface should show:
•	Move name
•	Element
•	Category
•	Power
•	Accuracy
•	Cooldown status
•	Short description
World abilities are separate from equipped combat moves.
A Hakko may know a world ability without using one of its six combat move slots.

20. STATUS EFFECTS
Support the following status effects:
•	Sleep
•	Freeze
•	Poison
•	Burn
•	Fear
•	Confusion
•	Blind
•	Silence
•	Paralysis
•	Bleeding
•	Curse
Each status should have a clear and distinct effect.
Suggested behaviours:
•	Sleep: unable to act for a limited number of turns, with a chance to wake.
•	Freeze: unable to act temporarily, with a chance to thaw.
•	Poison: loses HP at the end of each turn.
•	Burn: loses HP and suffers reduced physical attack.
•	Fear: chance to fail or use a weaker action.
•	Confusion: chance to damage itself or use an unintended move.
•	Blind: reduced accuracy.
•	Silence: cannot use special or status-category moves.
•	Paralysis: reduced speed and chance to lose a turn.
•	Bleeding: increasing or persistent physical damage over time.
•	Curse: long-duration debuff with an elementally themed penalty.
Do not make status effects overly complicated.
Display active statuses clearly in battle.
Camping and the Hakko Vet remove status effects.
Items may cure specific statuses.

21. BATTLE SYSTEM
Battles are turn-based.
Combat is 1v1 at any given time.
Each side may bring up to five Hakkos.
The active Hakko fights until:
•	It is switched
•	It faints
•	The battle ends
When a Hakko faints, the owner chooses the next available Hakko.
Switching Hakkos uses the player’s turn.
Speed normally determines action order.
Support:
•	Critical hits
•	Accuracy
•	Evasion where appropriate
•	Element multipliers
•	Status effects
•	Move cooldowns
•	Switching
•	Items
•	Capturing
•	Fleeing from wild encounters
•	Trainer and boss AI
Wild battles allow escape.
Arena and boss battles do not allow escape.
Trainer battles may allow surrender or may require defeat, depending on context.
The battle interface should show:
•	Player active Hakko
•	Enemy active Hakko
•	HP bars
•	Level
•	Element icons or labels
•	Status conditions
•	Available moves
•	Cooldowns
•	Switch option
•	Item option
•	Capture option in wild encounters
•	Run option in eligible encounters
•	Battle log or message area
The next Hakko should never be selected automatically after a faint unless only one remains.

22. BATTLE LOSS
The player does not lose money when defeated.
After losing:
•	Coal respawns at the most recently visited Hakko Vet.
•	The current battle ends.
•	The defeated trainer or boss remains undefeated.
•	The player may try again later.
•	Coal’s Hakkos are unavailable for a short recovery period.
For the tech demo, recovery may be represented by:
•	A short real-time timer
•	A limited number of world steps
•	A short in-game time period
•	A required rest interaction at the Vet
Do not make the recovery period frustrating.
The player should understand when each Hakko becomes available again.

23. TRAINER BEHAVIOUR
Use a mix of trainer interaction styles.
Some trainers should:
•	Approach Coal when Coal enters their detection area
•	Challenge Coal after brief dialogue
•	Allow Coal to refuse
•	Remain available for later battle
Other trainers should:
•	Stand in place
•	Only battle when spoken to
•	Offer advice before battle
•	Offer rematches after defeat
The player should usually be allowed to decline non-critical trainer battles.
Arena bosses may require confirmation before starting.
Arena trainers can be optional or required, but the route leading to each Arena should include several smaller battles.
A full production target is approximately ten minor trainer battles per unlocked region.
For the tech demo, include a representative number.

24. ARENAS
There are five main Arenas.
Each Arena boss specialises in one element.
Each boss should have:
•	Unique name
•	Distinct appearance
•	Personality
•	Short introductory dialogue
•	Signature Hakko
•	Themed battle music
•	Element-focused team
•	Trophy
•	Rematch dialogue
•	Region-appropriate difficulty
Use the following team-size progression:
•	Arena 1: 3 Hakkos
•	Arena 2: 4 Hakkos
•	Arena 3: 5 Hakkos
•	Arena 4: 5 Hakkos
•	Arena 5: 6 Hakkos
After defeat, Arena bosses offer rematches.
The player may decline.
Arena rematches can be accessed later.
Arena bosses should not use Legendary Hakkos.
Only the final twins use Legendary Hakkos in their regular teams.
Each town should contain NPC dialogue that hints at:
•	The next Arena’s specialisation
•	Useful elements
•	Useful status cures
•	Useful wild Hakkos nearby
This allows players to prepare without using external guides.

25. FINAL TWIN CHAMPIONS
Create two twin champions.
They should feel related but distinct.
Each twin should have:
•	Unique name
•	Distinct personality
•	Mixed-element team
•	Six Hakkos
•	One Legendary Hakko
•	A tactical identity
•	Separate battle dialogue
•	Defeat dialogue
•	Post-game clues
The battle format should remain 1v1.
Use two consecutive battles with a recovery opportunity only if appropriate.
A more dramatic option is:
1.	Battle Twin One.
2.	Short dialogue interlude.
3.	Limited or no free healing.
4.	Battle Twin Two.
Balance this fairly.
After both twins are defeated:
•	Coal becomes champion.
•	Coal receives recognition.
•	The final hidden Legendary quest unlocks.
•	The twins reveal an old journal or cryptic clue.
•	New NPC dialogue becomes available across the region.
•	The final Legendary’s location remains hidden until clues are followed.

26. WILD ENCOUNTERS
Wild Hakkos are visible in the world.
Do not use random encounters triggered by walking through grass.
Wild Hakkos should appear:
•	In bushes
•	In tall grass away from main paths
•	Near trees
•	In water
•	On beaches
•	In caves
•	Near ore deposits
•	On cliffs
•	In ruins
•	In hidden areas
•	At fishing spots
•	At mining spots
Do not place wild Hakkos directly on major roads unless the species is deliberately aggressive or roaming.
Wild Hakkos should use their temperament behaviours.
A battle begins when:
•	Coal interacts with a wild Hakko
•	An aggressive Hakko reaches Coal
•	A scripted encounter occurs
Allow visible Hakkos to respawn after time passes or after the player leaves and returns.
Rare and Legendary Hakkos should use longer respawn periods.

27. CAPTURE SYSTEM
Wild Hakkos are captured using consumable Tesseracts.
Each Tesseract holds one Hakko.
Tesseracts are folded pocket spaces designed to safely contain a willing or weakened Hakko.
Higher-quality Tesseracts are more stable and provide higher capture success.
Capture probability depends on:
•	Hakko current HP
•	Hakko maximum HP
•	Hakko rarity
•	Hakko level
•	Hakko status effects
•	Tesseract quality
•	Optional species-specific catch modifier
The player may throw a Tesseract at full HP, but the chance should be low.
Lower HP increases the chance.
Helpful status effects may increase capture chance.
When the player selects a Tesseract, show the current estimated capture percentage before confirmation.
Display this as an understandable percentage such as:
•	18%
•	47%
•	82%
Do not hide the capture chance.
Tesseracts are consumed when thrown, regardless of success.
Suggested Tesseract tiers:
•	Basic Tesseract
•	Stable Tesseract
•	Reinforced Tesseract
•	Refined Tesseract
•	Quantum Tesseract
•	Legendary-grade Tesseract, extremely limited
Better towns sell better Tesseracts as progression increases.
Some Tesseracts may also be awarded from quests.

28. ACTIVE DECK AND STORAGE
Coal may carry five active Hakkos.
Call this the Hakko Deck.
When Coal catches a Hakko while the deck has fewer than five members, the new Hakko may be added directly.
When the deck is full, ask the player to:
•	Replace one active Hakko
•	Send the new Hakko to home storage
Home storage is unlimited for practical purposes.
Storage should allow:
•	Viewing stored Hakkos
•	Viewing stats
•	Viewing elements
•	Viewing level
•	Viewing shiny status
•	Viewing moves
•	Adding a Hakko to the active deck
•	Removing a Hakko from the active deck
•	Selling duplicate or unwanted Hakkos
Do not allow the player to sell the last remaining example of a species without a clear warning.
Do not allow Legendary Hakkos to be sold.
The exact fictional explanation for selling Hakkos should remain humane.
For example, the player may transfer care rights to licensed handlers or sanctuaries rather than literally selling living creatures as objects.
The interface may still use the simple label “Transfer” or “Release for Reward” if that fits the world better.

29. HAKKO VET
Hakko Vets are the primary healing service.
They should:
•	Restore HP
•	Remove status effects
•	Revive fainted Hakkos
•	Manage defeat recovery
•	Provide storage access where appropriate
The service may be free or low-cost.
To avoid punishing players, basic healing should preferably be free.
The Vet should feel like a care facility rather than an impersonal machine.
Include a simple NPC attendant and healing feedback.

30. CAMPING
Camping is always available in safe outdoor areas.
Camping requires no gear.
Camping:
•	Restores 20% of each active Hakko’s maximum HP
•	Removes status effects
•	Does not revive fully fainted Hakkos unless deliberately balanced otherwise
•	May advance in-game time
•	Cannot be used during battle
•	Cannot be repeatedly abused without limitation
Use a simple limitation such as:
•	One camp per area visit
•	Short cooldown
•	Limited uses before visiting a town
•	Only usable outside dangerous zones
Keep the system convenient rather than punitive.

31. ITEMS AND INVENTORY
The inventory should focus on Hakko care and exploration.
Include:
•	Healing food
